note: The central PARADOXES and the PUNCTUMS of Ada Research's texts, made into stickers (2026-11-13). Seven readers read the walked prose (final.md), the wall texts and the framework and returned 112 candidates, each quote checked word for word; a truth critic and a sticker critic judged them in context; these 28 were chosen by hand, one per shared tension, across the spine. A paradox is two things a text holds true at once (a, b: the badge's paper and ink halves); a punctum (Barthes) is the detail that pricks (a: the caption under its photograph). 'quote' must stay word for word in 'file' or tools/stickers_seed.ts stops; 'line' is a reader's hint. Drawn by ada_encyclopedia src/lib/sticker-starter.ts (READING_MOTIFS[motif]).

readings.a: WE HAVE NOT DISPLAYED THAT LIMIT. WE HAVE MADE A FINITE INSTRUMENT…
readings.quote: The screen stops at five. Its smallest pieces still have width, height and depth. ... Its limiting set has zero total length and uncountably many points. We have not displayed that limit. We have made a finite instrument for approaching its rule.
readings.beyond: Only the mathematical construction, continued without a last cut, reaches a set of zero length and uncountably many points; a finite drawing can approach its rule but not show it.

readings.a: FROM THIS RECORD ALONE, WE CANNOT ASK WHETHER THE HAND MOVED … WITH DELIGHT.
readings.quote: The missing path saves work and storage. It also closes a question. From this record alone, we cannot ask whether the hand moved carefully, reluctantly or with delight. Increasing the precision of its final coordinates would not recover the movement.
readings.beyond: Keeping the hand's path, another version of the pose or the reason it was tried, though the text says none of these would keep the whole event.

readings.a: IT CANNOT DECIDE WHOSE BODY OUGHT TO BE THE MEASURE.
readings.quote: The code can name a clearance. It cannot decide whose body ought to be the measure.
readings.beyond: A judgement about whose body is the norm, which the code cannot make and which the visitor is left to weigh by widening the opening.

readings.a: NOTHING MEASURES 'HELD THE EDGE'... NO CLOCK AND NO ENDING
readings.quote: qfep_reactor is walkable but nothing measures 'held the edge' — the final test has no clock and no ending
readings.beyond: A clock on qfep_reactor that measures how long the edge was held, and an ending that follows from it; the log names this as the last open gap in the game's baseline.

readings.a: …WE MAY BEGIN LOOKING ONLY FOR THINGS THAT FIT THEM.
readings.quote: After enough time with these four rails, we may begin looking only for things that fit them. ... What have they made harder to think? What continues beyond their reach? The museum must be able to ask this of its own rooms, including this one.
readings.beyond: The museum asking of its own rooms, this one included, what the rails have made harder to think and what continues beyond their reach.

readings.a: WHAT THE BODY KNOWS AND THE BOOK CANNOT YET SAY
readings.quote: Palle's body-side registers (punctum/thrownness, ... the buzz/haptic, 'you are here', small/medium/large) did NOT fall out of ... the corpus — they live in VR and walked prose, not card text. ... the darkest fold: what the body knows and the book cannot yet say.
readings.beyond: A second, hand-named source of registers from walks in the headset, read against the measured matrix; where the two disagree is what the book has yet to learn to say.

readings.a: It fits a hand ... and nothing for a surface that carries a body
readings.quote: 8 term formulas say 'ground' or 'what you stand on' in plain words (field_terrain: 'the surface is also what you stand on'). The grammar has `hand` - it fits a hand, it can be taken - and nothing for a surface that carries a body.
readings.beyond: An operation for ground ('it fits a foot', a fourth level on the body axis, proposal p5) that Palle accepts and names.
